A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural network reduction framework. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. Proofs and experiments appearing in v2's main text can be matched to v3's Appendices A and B.

before.justification: Section V reports original image-verification experiments, ACAS Xu reduction and timing results, and closed-loop quadrotor evaluations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain original experiments and add verifier timing comparisons and large-perturbation robustness results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the initial upper bucket tolerance from 0.01 to max(uk) minus min(lk). The neuron-merging, look-ahead verification, compression, and reuse procedures otherwise remain substantially unchanged. Separating approximation intervals from biases reformulates the existing error treatment.

E1.justification: MNIST, CIFAR-10, ACAS Xu, and QUAD coverage is retained. Appendix B.2.5 adds large-perturbation verification scenarios on MNIST networks from the CORA benchmark, extending explicitly tested perturbations to epsilon = 0.1. This expands input-condition coverage without introducing a new image dataset.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds actual comparisons against alpha,beta-CROWN: CPU and GPU comparisons on the ERAN sigmoid network and a comparison on the Marabou CNN. v2 primarily measures reduced networks against their unreduced CORA counterparts; its references to DeepAbstract and INNAbstract discuss previously published results.

E3.justification: v3 adds cumulative-time-versus-verified-instance evaluations using fixed and automatically increased reduction rates, including CPU/GPU settings. Table 3 introduces standard, TRADES, and set-trained networks evaluated across larger perturbation radii. Table 1 also reports two post-convolution linear layers for Marabou, versus three in v2; this is a reported setting revision, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2.5 adds a robustness analysis of reduction at large perturbation radii across three training regimes. Most other analyses—reduction-rate and bucket-tolerance sensitivity, network-size variation, static versus dynamic buckets, compression, and network reuse—already appear in v2 and are reorganized into Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100-image averages, per-layer standard-deviation error bars, and ACAS Xu averages over 10 runs. However, v3 retains the shaded timing curves in Figure 8 while omitting v2's explicit identification of their shading as one standard deviation. No increased run count or new seed information is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds comparative timing results: v3 reports approximately 200 ms CPU verification for most ERAN instances at rho = 0.1, alongside CROWN timings of 4.5 s on CPU and 1.5 s on GPU, and a 30% overall Marabou timing advantage. Table 3 adds large-radius reduction results, including 0.3556 for set-trained MNIST at epsilon = 0.1. The earlier ERAN sensitivity and ACAS Xu tables retain their numerical results as Tables 2 and 4.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds an asymptotic overhead argument for Algorithm 2 and expands Theorem 1's proof to distinguish exact-set inclusion from separately computed outer approximations. Corollary 1 changes the compression kernel from three channels to an arbitrary input-channel count. Most other proofs and convolutional derivations are relocated existing material.

C1.justification: The central claims of sound, automatic, input-specific reduction for general activation functions remain. v3 drops the broad CNN-priority claim from the contributions and emphasizes time-critical verification, adding claims of up to 96% shorter verification time and individual layers up to an order of magnitude larger than entire networks considered by prior reduction studies.

C2.justification: v3 adds an overparameterization-based interpretation of network-size results, explains the large-radius applicability boundary through standard versus robustly trained networks, and discusses why additive errors integrate more easily into existing verifiers than interval weights. Conversely, v2's detailed interpretation of differing sigmoid/ReLU bucket-tolerance behavior is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds GPU hardware information and an architecture-summary table, but removes several explicit epsilon/delta settings for retained experiments, detailed activation-error bounding instructions, and the planned CORA-release statement. Table 1 also lists ACAS-XU as 7 x 50, conflicting with the retained 6 x 50 hidden-layer description in B.3.2. These documentation changes do not establish changed code availability or experimental reruns.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially revised around time-critical verification and scalability. Related work adds bisimulation-based reduction, earlier CNN abstraction, additional interval-network work and a review, plus formal-XAI, robust-training, and 2024 competition references. Acknowledging Ostrovsky et al.'s CNN work accompanies the narrower novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, contributions, evaluation narrative, and conclusion are extensively revised. The evaluation is reorganized around comparative timing results, while existing benchmark discussions become appendix ablations and supplementary experiments. Proofs move to Appendix A, preliminary definitions are consolidated, and application subsections are reordered.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 combines six panels into three, and Figure 3 replaces a generic network diagram with an annotated numerical example. Existing plots are combined into Figures 7 and 10 or relocated to the appendix; new timing plots and architecture/robustness tables are added.

improvement.justification: The direct CROWN comparisons, large-perturbation experiments, clearer merging example, and acknowledgment of earlier CNN reduction make v3 more informative about practical value and novelty. These gains are partly offset by lost experimental settings, underspecified perturbations in the new timing comparisons, and inconsistent architecture descriptions. The evidence supports a useful but limited net improvement.
